Based on the retrieved matches, it appears that routine insertion of an endoscopic biliary drainage (ENBD) tube is not beneficial in patients with choledocholithiasis-induced cholangitis. A routinely inserted ENBD tube did not improve the clinical course and was found to be unnecessary.

In fact, a study found that the insertion would actually be counterproductive, requiring increased procedure time and discomfort for patients. This suggests that routine insertion of an ENBD tube is not necessary in these cases, especially considering that the tube may cause more harm than good.

Therefore, it is recommended that patients with choledocholithiasis-induced cholangitis who undergo endoscopic clearance of the common bile duct do not require a routinely inserted ENBD tube.
